summary: Spiridon Dmitrievič Èl’manovič worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1865 to 1869 and served as director of Kholm Gymnasium in 1896.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD ~2011–2016). She has held posts at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, Harvard's CSWR, and the University of Houston.

Sravani Kanamarlapudi works in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Texas at Austin as a PhD student around 2018, at the University of Washington in 2019, and under Richard G. Salomon.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Visva-Bharati University, Andhra University, and the University of Marburg (PhD ~1963–1966). He served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1977 to 1997.
Sri Anirvan was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed his studies at Sanskrit College and University (~1914–1916), the University of Calcutta (~1916–1918), and the University of Dhaka.

Sri Aurobindo was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at St Paul's School, King's College, Cambridge, and under Robert Mason Towers, Dinendra Kumar Ray, and Vishnu Bhaskar Lele. He taught at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1893–1906).

Srikanth Kaul was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. In 1967, he was attested at Government Degree College, Sopore, and as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.

Srimanta Bhadra is a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Bhadra earned a PhD from Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute by 2021 and became an assistant professor at Raja Narendra Lal Khan Women's College in 2017.

Srinivas H. Ritti was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as an epigraphical assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1964) and Government Epigraphist for India (1965), and later as professor at Karnatak University (1975).

Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Hamburg (~1962–1967). He served as Privatdozent für Indologie at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.
Srinivasa Kumar N Acharya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned an MA at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha and was appointed assistant professor at Manipal Academy of Higher Education in 2011.

Sriram Krishnan works in computational linguistics and Indology. Krishnan has held academic posts at Central Sanskrit University, the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad, and the University of Hyderabad.

Sriram Subramanian works in Indology and computational fields. He studied at Pondicherry Engineering College, University of Cincinnati, Hindu University of America (PhD 2019), and MIT Group of Institutions, and became a principal software engineer at Microsoft in 2022.

Srisa Chandra Vasu was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Rang Mahal Mission High School and Government College University, Lahore. He founded the Panini Office (1891), served as a Vakil at Allahabad High Court (~1888–1893), and was a fellow at Allahabad University.

Stacey Boulter works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at Dalhousie University (BA 2016–2025) and McMaster University (MA 2025), where she also served as a teaching assistant in 2025.

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Sinology. She studied under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, earning degrees from the University of Colorado Boulder and Columbia University (PhD attested 2006; post attested 2013).

Stamford Raffles worked in history, linguistics, and other fields. Employed by the East India Company (~1795–1824), he was Chief Secretary of Prince of Wales Island (1807), Governor of Java (~1811–1816), and founder and president of the Zoological Society of London.

Stanford E. Lehmberg was a historian who earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge under Christopher Morris (~1954–1956). He served as an emeritus professor at the University of Minnesota from around 1999 to 2012.
Stanislao Gatti was an Italian scholar of philosophy and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Naples Federico II and held a post there from around 1861 to 1870.

Stanislas Guyard was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from 1868 and became Professor of Arabic at the Collège de France in 1884.
